title: Signature Arithmetic Drills
description: A Signature-original drill set for arithmetic fluency: timed factor ladders, remainder races, and ratio sprints, each scored against the learner's own last attempt rather than any external bar. The drill doctrine is that arithmetic must be automatic before algebra begins — hesitation at this level compounds into failure later. Signature-original, labeled Signature.

score = sum(1 for a, b in [(7,8),(12,12),(9,6)] if True)
print('drill: 7x8, 12x12, 9x6 -> answers 56, 144, 54')
print('doctrine: automatic recall before algebra; beat your own last score')

title: Signature Trig Circle Walk
description: A Signature-original drill: walk the unit circle degree by degree, calling out sine and cosine from the coordinates until the special angles are reflex. The walk replaces memorized tables with a single image — the circle — from which every identity is re-derived on demand. Signature-original.

for deg in (0, 30, 45, 60, 90):
    r = math.radians(deg)
    print(f'{deg} deg -> (cos, sin) = ({round(math.cos(r),3)}, {round(math.sin(r),3)})')

title: Signature Chance Simulator
description: A Signature-original simulator-first approach to probability: run ten thousand trials of any chance question before computing the theory, so intuition is calibrated by experience. The simulator exposes the gambler's fallacy, the base-rate fallacy, and overconfidence in small samples as lived experience. Signature-original.
demo:
import random
random.seed(3)
runs = sum(random.random() < 0.5 for _ in range(10000))
print('simulated P(heads) ~', round(runs/10000, 3))
print('simulate first (10k trials), theorize second')

title: Signature Rate Lab
description: A Signature-original lab for differential equations: simulate cooling coffee, a falling object, and a spreading rumor with Euler's method before meeting any analytic technique. The lab teaches that most real equations are solved numerically, and analytic solutions are the lucky exceptions. Signature-original.
demo:
T, room, k, dt = 90.0, 22.0, 0.05, 1.0
for _ in range(10): T -= k*(T-room)*dt
print('coffee after 10 min ~', round(T,1), 'C (Euler on Newton cooling)')
print('most real equations are solved numerically; analytic = lucky')

title: Signature Error Budget
description: A Signature-original discipline from numerical analysis: every computation carries an error budget — rounding, truncation, and conditioning — written down before the code runs. The discipline's exercise is to break a naive algorithm on purpose (catastrophic cancellation) and then fix it. Signature-original.
